title: 13 Best AI App Builders with Built-In User Authentication in 2027
summary: Building apps with secure user authentication is increasingly important for founders and small businesses. According to Verizon's 2025 research…
body_markdown:
Building apps with secure user authentication is increasingly important for founders and small businesses. According to Verizon's 2025 research, credential-stuffing attacks accounted for a median of[19% of daily authentication](https://www.verizon.com/business/resources/articles/credential-stuffing-attacks-2025-dbir-research/) attempts in the single sign-on provider logs analyzed. This highlights why reliable login systems matter when creating customer portals, SaaS products, and internal business applications.


For teams planning projects in 2027, AI app builders can simplify authentication setup through built-in login features and managed infrastructure. Platforms like[Floot](https://floot.com/) provide email/password authentication and managed Google and Microsoft sign-in alongside databases and hosting. This guide compares 13 AI app builders based on authentication capabilities, security controls, setup complexity, and pricing, using product information available as of November 15, 2026.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Managed authentication:**[Floot's sign-in system](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/app-sign-in) supports email/password accounts, password resets, and brokered Google and Microsoft OAuth without separate OAuth app registration.
- **AI-assisted development:** Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) lets supported AI assistants create, edit, and publish applications while Floot manages the infrastructure. Available actions depend on connector permissions and client capabilities.
- **Integrated backend:** Floot combines authentication with[managed Postgres](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) , serverless backend endpoints, hosting, and file storage. Application-level authorization checks control access to user-specific records.
- **Transparent pricing:** Floot is free to start. Its[pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) offer 100 daily build actions on Free, 1,000 on Pro, and 5,000 on Power, with separate allowances for hosting and optional AI features.
- **Mobile deployment:** Floot's[mobile app capabilities](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) let teams convert web applications into installable iOS and Android apps, subject to plan allowances and applicable developer-account requirements.


## **What to Look For in an AI App Builder with Built-In Authentication**


Choosing an AI app builder with authentication depends on the application's audience, security requirements, and expected usage. A small customer portal may only need email/password login and basic permissions, while an enterprise dashboard may require SSO, audit logging, and granular access controls. Before selecting a platform, evaluate these capabilities:


- **Authentication methods:** Look for email/password login, Google or Microsoft OAuth, magic links, phone verification, and enterprise SSO where required. Confirm which methods are built in and which require separate identity-provider configuration. Floot's[authentication documentation](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/app-sign-in) explains its supported login methods.
- **Security and compliance:** Check current SOC 2 Type II audit status, GDPR-related controls, HIPAA support where applicable, and plan-specific security features. Confirm whether authentication includes password protection, session management, and access logging.
- **Setup complexity:** Some builders require OAuth credentials, redirect URIs, or external authentication services. Others manage these configurations directly. Non-technical teams should prioritize clear setup instructions and minimal manual configuration.
- **User limits and pricing:** Compare authenticated-user limits across Free and paid plans. Check whether pricing depends on users, builders, workspaces, application usage, or hosting consumption. Review[Floot's pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) for its build-action limits and hosting allowances.
- **Database integration and access control:** Authentication should connect user identities to stored records. Verify whether row-level restrictions are enforced by the database, application backend, or platform permissions. Floot's[managed Postgres](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) and[security documentation](https://floot.com/docs/platform/security-and-data) explain its data infrastructure and security controls.
- **Mobile compatibility:** Teams building iOS and Android apps should verify supported login methods, Apple Sign-In requirements where applicable, and whether mobile publishing requires additional developer accounts. Floot's[mobile app documentation](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) explains its mobile-building and publishing workflows.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations.


Floot provides managed infrastructure while the connected AI assistant handles development, with available building capabilities depending on the client's connector permissions. The platform is designed for non-technical founders, business owners, and operators who need working applications with authentication, persistent data, and hosting rather than static prototypes.


### **Why It Fits Teams Building Secure Applications**


Floot provides built-in email/password authentication for app users and brokers Google and Microsoft OAuth sign-in without requiring separate OAuth app registration. Users can ask a connected AI assistant to add login functionality. Floot supports the underlying application infrastructure, including database-backed user accounts, sessions, and authentication workflows.


The platform also supports additional OAuth providers such as Apple using app-registered credentials. These integrations require the appropriate provider configuration and should be tested before launch.


### **Authentication and Security Capabilities**


- Built-in[email/password authentication](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/app-sign-in) for application users
- Google and Microsoft OAuth brokering without separate OAuth app registration
- Support for Apple and other identity providers using app-registered OAuth credentials
- Managed Postgres databases that store application user accounts and related data
- Password reset workflows and account lockout protections
- Secure browser-based handling of third-party credentials
- Backend authorization logic for controlling access to user-specific records


### **What Makes Floot Different**


Floot's primary differentiator is its ability to use supported AI assistants for development while providing the managed infrastructure required to run applications. Its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) lets users work through familiar tools instead of requiring a separate development environment. The assistant handles application development, while Floot provides authentication, hosting, database services, and deployment.


Connector-based building uses the user's existing AI subscription rather than consuming Floot AI credits for model tokens. Floot meters platform operations through build actions, while hosting and optional AI features have separate usage rules. For additional context, Floot's[Lovable comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-lovable-compare-ai-no-code-platforms-2025) ,[Replit comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-replit-compare-ai-vibecoding-platforms-in-2026) , and[Base44 alternatives](https://floot.com/blog/base44-alternatives) explain different app-building and infrastructure approaches.


### **Pricing and Getting Started**


Floot is free to start, with three main plans:


- **Free:** $0/month, 100 daily build actions, a one-time $3 hosting credit at signup, and 2 mobile app builds per month.
- **Pro:** $25/month, 1,000 daily build actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, a $10 monthly hosting allowance, and 12 mobile app builds per month.
- **Power:** $100/month, 5,000 daily build actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, a $25 monthly hosting allowance, and unlimited mobile app builds.


These are monthly billing prices. Annual billing provides two months free. Hosting usage beyond included allowances draws from prepaid hosting credit, and optional auto-reload is off by default. Existing AI assistant subscriptions are billed separately from Floot. AI credits support optional Floot AI features and the Floot agent, rather than connector-based model tokens. Users own their application code and data on every plan. Database export is available on all plans, while full project ZIP download requires a paid plan. Teams can explore[Floot's integrations](https://floot.com/en/integrations) to understand how authentication works alongside payments, email, storage, and other application services.


## **2. Softr**


Softr is a no-code business app builder that creates applications with built-in authentication, native databases, and optional connections to Airtable and Google Sheets.


### **Primary Focus**


Softr works well for teams building client portals, internal directories, membership sites, and data-connected applications. Its interface and data management tools are designed for business users who want to create and manage operational applications without traditional coding.


### **Authentication Capabilities**


- Email/password login across plans
- Google sign-in and one-time-code authentication on eligible higher-tier plans
- User groups and permissions with record-level data restrictions
- SOC 2 Type II compliance and GDPR-related controls
- SAML and OpenID Connect SSO on Enterprise
- 5 authenticated app users on the Free plan


### **App Building Considerations**


Softr's authentication is integrated with its data connection layer. Users can be managed within Softr or synchronized with connected data sources, including Airtable and Google Sheets. Teams should verify their plan's authentication methods and user-group limits before deployment.


### **Organizational Fit**


Paid plans start at $25/month with monthly billing or $19/month when billed annually. The Free plan supports up to 5 app users, while higher plans provide additional user allowances and advanced authentication features.


## **3. Base44**


Base44 is an AI-powered web app builder acquired by Wix in 2025. It combines native database support, authentication, and application-building tools in one platform.


### **Primary Focus**


Base44 is relevant for teams that want all-in-one functionality without manually connecting separate database, authentication, and hosting services. The platform provides built-in login and user management alongside database and application-generation features.


### **Authentication Capabilities**


- Built-in login and user management
- Authentication connected to application database records
- Security scanning tools for identifying potential application vulnerabilities
- Native database support
- Application-level permissions and access controls


### **App Building Considerations**


Base44 has been owned by Wix since June 2025. Its integrated development environment supports authentication and database workflows without requiring users to assemble a separate backend stack. Application permissions and security settings should still be reviewed before publication.


### **Organizational Fit**


The Free plan supports up to 5 applications. Paid plans start at $16/month when billed annually or $20/month with monthly billing.


## **4. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets users build and publish interactive websites and lightweight web applications through ChatGPT, with built-in storage and optional Sign in with ChatGPT.


### **Primary Focus**


ChatGPT Sites is relevant for individuals and teams already using ChatGPT who want to create dashboards, client-facing tools, or interactive websites without setting up a separate development environment.


### **Authentication Capabilities**


- Optional Sign in with ChatGPT for visitor accounts and saved progress
- Built-in database and file storage for application data
- Sharing controls for private, workspace-restricted, and public access
- Support for application-specific access rules and personalized experiences


### **App Building Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites supports built-in storage and authentication through ChatGPT identities. Public Sites can offer optional visitor sign-in, while workspace-restricted Sites use workspace access controls. Teams needing specific OAuth identity providers or advanced authentication workflows should verify compatibility before publishing.


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites is available on eligible paid ChatGPT plans, with usage, storage, and publishing limits depending on plan and workspace settings. Building and editing Sites counts toward applicable Codex usage allowances.


## **5. ToolJet**


ToolJet is an open-source enterprise internal tool builder with authentication and access-control capabilities.


### **Primary Focus**


ToolJet is an option for enterprise teams that need configurable permissions, SSO integration, and audit logging. It supports cloud and self-hosted deployment options, allowing organizations to choose how they manage application infrastructure.


### **Authentication Capabilities**


- SSO through SAML, OIDC, and LDAP on eligible Team and Enterprise plans
- Granular page-, component-, and query-level access rules on Enterprise
- Workspace and application-level permissions
- Directory groups that can map onto ToolJet roles
- Audit logs on Team and Enterprise plans, with retention varying by plan
- SOC 2 Type II and GDPR-related security controls


### **App Building Considerations**


ToolJet combines visual application building with AI-assisted generation and enterprise access controls. Advanced permissions, SSO, and audit logging are plan-dependent rather than universally included.


### **Organizational Fit**


ToolJet Cloud offers a Free plan supporting up to 2 builders and 50 end users. Paid Basic plans start at $23/builder/month with annual billing. Team and Enterprise plans provide additional security and governance features.


## **6. Zite**


Zite is a no-code business software builder that offers unlimited application users on every plan, including Free.


### **Primary Focus**


Zite is relevant for teams that need applications serving many authenticated users without per-seat pricing. The platform includes application generation, database functionality, and user management tools.


### **Authentication Capabilities**


- Built-in authentication with user permissions
- Unlimited users and applications across plans
- SSO for app users on Enterprise
- Granular permissions and role-based access on Team plans
- SOC 2 Type II compliance
- No per-seat pricing model


### **App Building Considerations**


Zite's pricing model can suit applications with large numbers of users. Teams requiring advanced role configuration or enterprise identity management should evaluate the relevant higher-tier plans.


### **Organizational Fit**


Paid Pro plans start at $20/month when billed annually or $25/month with monthly billing. The Free plan includes unlimited users and apps, subject to usage, database-record, and credit limits.


## **7. Replit**


Replit is a cloud-based development environment with an AI Agent that can build full-stack applications and implement authentication workflows.


### **Primary Focus**


Replit is relevant for teams that want a development environment combining application code, databases, deployment, and AI-assisted programming. The platform supports traditional coding workflows alongside agent-generated application development.


### **Authentication Capabilities**


- Replit Auth for supported authentication workflows
- Support for implementing third-party authentication providers
- Managed PostgreSQL databases for persistent application data
- AI Agent assistance with login and authorization code
- Integration of authentication with full-stack application logic


### **App Building Considerations**


Replit supports app publishing alongside managed database and authentication capabilities. Application developers can inspect and modify generated authentication code. Authentication and authorization logic should be tested before production deployment.


### **Organizational Fit**


The Free Starter plan includes one published application, with free publishing limited to 30 days before republishing is required. Core starts at $20/month with monthly billing or $18/month when billed annually.


## **8. Lovable**


Lovable is a full-stack AI web app builder that generates React applications with authentication supported through its cloud backend and integrations.


### **Primary Focus**


Lovable is relevant for teams building web applications through natural-language prompts. It generates user interfaces and connects them to backend services that support persistent data and user accounts.


### **Authentication Capabilities**


- Lovable Cloud backend with built-in authentication
- Supabase-powered authentication options
- Full-stack React generation with login and signup interfaces
- GitHub synchronization for application source code
- Support for application code export through available workflows


### **App Building Considerations**


Lovable generates application interfaces and can connect them to database and authentication services. Teams should verify how authentication, database configuration, and row-level security policies are implemented before publishing applications with sensitive user data.


### **Organizational Fit**


The Free plan includes 5 build credits per day, capped at 30 per month, alongside separate Cloud and AI feature allowances. Pro plans start at $25/month.


## **9. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new is a browser-based AI code generator from StackBlitz that runs Node.js development environments through WebContainers technology.


### **Primary Focus**


Bolt.new is relevant for developers and technical teams who want to inspect and modify generated authentication code. Its browser-based environment supports full-stack application development without requiring a traditional local setup.


### **Authentication Capabilities**


- Authentication workflows implemented through prompting
- Database security checks available across plans
- Optional full security audits on paid plans
- Native database support with hosting
- Node.js development environments
- Application source code access and export workflows


### **App Building Considerations**


Bolt.new supports full-stack application development with authentication implemented through generated code. Teams should test login, session management, and authorization behavior before publishing. Full project security audits are available on paid plans.


### **Organizational Fit**


The Free plan includes 1 million tokens per month, with a daily limit of 300,000 tokens. Pro plans start at $25/month with monthly billing.


## **10. Retool**


Retool is an internal tool builder designed for developers who need to create admin panels, dashboards, and operational applications with authentication.


### **Primary Focus**


Retool is an option for engineering teams building internal applications. It provides SQL-level control over data access and security features for internal tool management.


### **Authentication Capabilities**


- Version release controls
- Role-based access control with plan-dependent permissions
- SSO, SCIM, and 2FA on Enterprise plans
- SQL-level control over application data access
- Unlimited applications on the Free plan, with up to 5 users


### **App Building Considerations**


Retool's Free plan can suit small teams creating internal dashboards and administrative tools. More advanced authentication, governance, and external-user features require higher-tier plans.


### **Organizational Fit**


Team pricing starts at $10/builder/month plus $5/internal user/month when billed annually. The Free plan supports up to 5 users, while Enterprise plans provide additional identity-management capabilities.


## **11. Glide**


Glide turns spreadsheet and database information into mobile-friendly business applications with authentication and access-control features.


### **Primary Focus**


Glide is relevant for teams creating business applications from connected data sources, including Google Sheets and Airtable. Its visual building environment helps users produce internal tools and mobile-friendly applications.


### **Authentication Capabilities**


- SSO capabilities on Enterprise
- Role-based access and row-level permissions
- SOC 2 and GDPR-related security controls
- Encryption and managed application access controls
- User authentication connected to application data


### **App Building Considerations**


Glide provides authentication and permissions for applications built from connected data. Enterprise security features and access-control capabilities vary by plan.


### **Organizational Fit**


Basic plans start at $25/month and include personal or team app publishing. Public application publishing requires the Plus plan, starting at $50/month.


## **12. Knack**


Knack is a no-code database application builder with a pricing model that does not charge separately for every application user.


### **Primary Focus**


Knack is relevant for teams building applications with many authenticated users, such as customer portals, membership directories, and service catalogs. Its pricing model uses subscription tiers with application and database-record limits rather than per-user charges.


### **Authentication Capabilities**


- User management without per-seat pricing
- Flexible user roles and permissions
- GDPR-related data controls
- HIPAA-related hosting options on eligible plans with appropriate agreements
- SSO integration on eligible higher-tier plans
- Customer-facing portal authentication


### **App Building Considerations**


Knack's pricing can suit applications with large user populations. The platform provides built-in authentication and role-based access, with dedicated options for regulated industries subject to plan requirements, contractual terms, and configuration.


### **Organizational Fit**


The Starter plan costs $59/month with monthly billing or $49/month when billed annually. It includes unlimited application users and roles, subject to plan-specific database and usage limits.


## **13. FlutterFlow**


FlutterFlow is a visual builder for Flutter mobile applications with Firebase authentication integration.


### **Primary Focus**


FlutterFlow is an option for teams building native iOS and Android applications that require mobile-specific authentication patterns. Its visual development tools support mobile application design, backend connections, and deployment workflows.


### **Authentication Capabilities**


- Firebase Authentication integration
- Email/password, Google, Apple Sign-In, and phone authentication
- Native iOS and Android authentication patterns
- Full source code export on eligible paid plans
- Firebase and Supabase support for database and storage integrations


### **App Building Considerations**


FlutterFlow provides mobile authentication workflows with Firebase support for authentication, databases, and storage. Teams publishing iOS applications should confirm applicable Apple Sign-In requirements and test authentication behavior on supported devices.


### **Organizational Fit**


The Free plan includes up to 2 projects. Paid Basic plans start at $39/month with monthly billing.


## **Why Floot Stands Out for Built-In User Authentication**


Floot connects[managed authentication](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/app-sign-in) with full-stack infrastructure, letting non-technical teams build applications through supported AI assistants. Instead of configuring separate hosting, database, and authentication services, users can describe their requirements while Floot provides the infrastructure behind the application.


Key capabilities include:


- **Managed OAuth:** Google and Microsoft sign-in without separate OAuth app registration.
- **Persistent data:**[Postgres databases](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) for storing user accounts and application records.
- **Access control:** Backend authorization checks for user-specific data.
- **Mobile deployment:**[iOS and Android builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) with authentication carried into the application.
- **Code ownership:** Project ownership on every plan, with downloadable ZIP exports on paid plans.


Floot is particularly relevant for founders building MVPs, customer portals, and business tools. Its[connector workflow](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) supports development through familiar AI assistants while hosting, database management, and deployment remain integrated. Mobile store publishing still requires developer accounts and store approval.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is built-in user authentication in AI app builders?**


Built-in authentication means an application builder provides login capabilities without requiring every authentication component to be developed from scratch. This may include email/password login, OAuth providers, password resets, session management, and user permissions. Capabilities vary by platform and plan. For example,[Floot's authentication](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/app-sign-in) includes database-backed user accounts, email/password sessions, and brokered Google and Microsoft sign-in.


### **How does Floot handle user authentication for applications?**


Floot provides email/password authentication, password reset workflows, and Google and Microsoft OAuth sign-in without separate OAuth app registration. When an authorized AI assistant is asked to add login, Floot supports the required application infrastructure, including user-account tables, backend functionality, and sessions. Additional providers such as Apple can be integrated using the app owner's OAuth credentials. Teams can review the[authentication documentation](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/app-sign-in) for setup details.


### **Are there additional costs for built-in authentication features?**


Authentication pricing varies between platforms. Some offer authentication within free plans but restrict user counts or advanced identity providers. Others charge based on application users, builders, or usage. Floot includes authentication as part of its managed infrastructure. Its[pricing structure](https://floot.com/en/pricing) separates build-action allowances, hosting usage, and optional AI features. Floot is free to start, while Pro costs $25/month and includes a $10 monthly hosting allowance.


### **Can custom identity providers be integrated with AI app builders?**


Many app builders support common OAuth providers, including Google and Microsoft. Enterprise platforms may also offer SAML, OpenID Connect, or directory-based SSO. Floot brokers Google and Microsoft sign-in directly. Apple and other supported OAuth providers can be integrated using the app owner's registered credentials. For external services, Floot provides[integration guidance](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/overview) covering authentication credentials and secure configuration.


### **Does Floot support mobile authentication and advanced security requirements?**


Floot supports email/password login and Google and Microsoft OAuth in applications that can also be packaged for iOS and Android. Apple Sign-In can be implemented with the application's own OAuth credentials. Teams requiring MFA, passwordless login, or enterprise SSO for their app users should verify the exact implementation and relevant provider requirements before deployment. Floot's[mobile documentation](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) explains build allowances, developer-account requirements, and publishing workflows. Store approval is subject to Apple and Google review.
